Subject: DPA / SCCs redlines — decision cadence and escalation plan

Team —

Thanks for sending the initial order form back last week. As we prepare to finalize the MSA + Order Form for Acme Health, I want to propose a tight cadence for the outstanding DPA and SCCs redlines so we can meet the procurement deadline on July 6. Key asks up front:

- Can counsel provide a single redline (tracked) for the DPA + a separate PDF for the SCCs annex by end of day Thursday (Ellen)?
- We need a short decision matrix from Redwood on the top 5 negotiable items vs non-negotiable items by Monday (internal).
- If there are any delegation/processor role questions that affect hosting (VPC vs hosted), flag them immediately — this will change scope.

Proposed cadence:
- Thu 6/25 EOD: External redline received (DPA_Redline_v2 + SCCs_Annex)
- Fri 6/26 morning: Internal legal + product quick triage (30m) to prioritize must-haves vs asks
- Mon 6/29: Draft response redline sent back to Acme with fallback language for SLO/hosting carveouts
- Tue 6/30: Final alignment and signoff path (Laura to approve any exceptions)

Olga / Marissa — please confirm availability for the Fri AM triage and list any technical evidence we may need to prepare (KMS attestations, data residency runbook). Ellen / Acme — once we have your redline we'll call out items that require operational changes.

Ben

Subject: Re: DPA / SCCs redlines — decision cadence and escalation plan

Ben / team —

Thanks, attached is our redline set. High level: we kept most standard clauses but added three asks that will likely be sticking points for Acme —

1) Data export & routing: request for binding statement that processing will not transfer outside EU/US without prior notice; prefers express SCC mapping in annex.
2) Subprocessor flow-down: asks for right-to-audit of key subprocessor certs (SOC2 + KMS attest).
3) Liability cap carveout for security incidents tied to gross negligence (counsel wants to preserve carveout language).

We've included tracked changes: DPA_Redline_v2.docx and a clean SCCs_Annex.pdf. We flagged the processor/controller role table (section 4) with comments — this is the area that will require product/ops confirmation about where workloads can be hosted.

If you want, we can hop on a 20-minute call Fri morning to walk through the redline line-by-line.

Best,
Ellen Santos
Finsley LLP — Health & Privacy Practice

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 07:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA / SCCs redlines — decision cadence and escalation plan

Looping internal notes into the thread after a quick triage with infra and product. Quick summary of impact and asks (see redline-summary.xlsx for line refs):

- Hosting & transfers: Counsel's request to lock processing to US/EU unless notified is operationally acceptable for hosted Redwood, but causes complications for Dedicated/Private where customers may choose APAC regions. Product asks for a scoped exception: allow customer-chosen region with explicit opt-in on Order Form. Decision: is Acme willing to accept region opt-in vs blanket restriction?

- Subprocessor audit right: Engineering flagged that providing audit rights for some third-party infra vendors is feasible but must be scoped (e.g., SOC2/ISO certs only, not ad hoc penetration tests). Proposed language: "reasonable evidence of third-party certifications on request". Need legal concurrence.

- Liability carveout: Business wants to keep standard cap but accept a narrowly drawn carveout for proven gross negligence with an upper bound tied to the order form value. Ask: Laura to confirm tolerance for a partial carveout here.

Next actions I recommend:
1) Laura to approve negotiation floor for liability carveouts and region opt-in approach (cc'd).
2) Ben to propose the specific Order Form opt-in wording for region selection (I'll help draft).
3) Legal to prepare a one-page negotiation memo to send Acme that lists fallback language for the 3 items above.

I'll attach our quick redline sheet (redline-summary.xlsx) with clause numbers and suggested fallback phrasing. If no objections I'll prepare the draft memo for review this afternoon.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: DPA / SCCs redlines — decision cadence and escalation plan

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. Laura, quick ask: can you confirm by EOD whether we have latitude for the targeted liability carveout and the region opt-in (we'd like to provide Acme with a clear alternative rather than a hard no). If Laura approves, Marissa and I will finalize the one-page negotiation memo and Ben will send to Acme with a short note on operational guardrails.

Operational notes for the memo:
- KMS evidence: offer specific attestation (HSM/KMS model + certs) and a SOC2 snapshot rather than live audits.
- Region opt-in wording (proposed): "Customer may elect specific processing regions at time of Order Form execution; Redwood will not move processing to a different jurisdiction without prior written notice and Customer consent, except as required by law." (we can tighten language if Laura asks)
- Liability fallback: propose cap tied to 12 months of committed fees for the Order Form line item; carveout limited to proven gross negligence and with required escalation to legal before release.

If no escalation from Laura, Ben please schedule the send to Acme for Mon 6/29 morning. Ellen — can you confirm if Acme will accept a scoped SOC2 evidence flow instead of open audit rights? That will speed things.

Olga
